title: Rollouts: add standardized SLO dashboards (latency/error) + alert templates for auto-rollback
author: Sergio Costa
body:
Summary: This PR adds a standardized set of Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert templates for rollout SLO monitoring (latency + error) that the rollout-controller will reference for auto-rollback decisioning and operator workflows. The goal is to make the signals consistent across route/model/region/tier and to provide a single source of truth for the monitor identity contract and query shapes.

Context: The auto-rollback project (ENG-2312/2314/2315) needs stable monitor identities and predictable queries to determine whether a canary/AB rollout is breaching SLOs. This PR implements the “rollout SLO” dashboard set and alert rules that match the canonical labels from ADR-0147 (route, model, region, customer_tier, deployment_mode) and are designed to avoid false positives during warm-up and low traffic.

What’s included: 1) Dashboards: - "Rollouts / SLO Overview" (high-level: latency + error across rollout candidates vs baseline) - "Rollouts / SLO Drilldown" (route+model breakdown with per-region and per-tier splits) - "Rollouts / Monitor Health" (monitor freshness, query errors, missing labels, sample counts) 2) Panels (shared across dashboards): - Latency: p50/p95/p99 (ms), with baseline overlay (stable version) - Error: request error-rate (5xx + gateway errors) and availability %, with burn-rate style view (short/long windows) - Traffic qualification: requests/min, token throughput, sample size gate (to debug min-traffic guardrails) - Region comparison: small multiples per region to spot localized capacity/network issues - Rollout annotations: rollout start/step changes + rollback events (fed from audit event stream where available; otherwise a placeholder annotation query) 3) Alert templates (PrometheusRule / jsonnet templates): - RolloutSLOLatencyBreach (warn/page variants) - RolloutSLOErrorBreach (warn/page variants) - RolloutSLOMonitorStale (ticket; not paged by default) - RolloutSLOLabelMissing (ticket; helps migration to ADR-0147) These templates are parameterized by route/model/region/tier and intentionally include a traffic qualifier (min req rate) to reduce flapping.

Key design choices / guardrails: - Label contract alignment: All queries are keyed on {route, model, region, customer_tier, deployment_mode}. Where older metrics expose service/endpoint instead of route, we use the normalization helper to map -> route, and we surface a "label missing" panel to force visibility during migration (ENG-2322). - Low traffic handling: Default alert expressions include a minimum request rate gate and a minimum sample count gate (requests in window) to avoid triggering on sparse routes. Operators can still view the raw series in the drilldown dashboard. - Warm-up exclusion: Dashboards include a variable "rollout_age" and a panel note; alerts ship with a default “ignore first N minutes” option via a recording rule that gates on rollout_start_timestamp when present. If rollout metadata isn’t present, we fall back to request-rate ramp detection (documented in the dashboard description). - Baseline comparison: Dashboards show candidate vs stable overlays. Alerts remain absolute-threshold by default (to avoid baseline instability), but the template supports an optional "must_be_worse_than_baseline" clause for use by rollout-controller policies.

How rollout-controller will reference this: - The dashboard UIDs and panel IDs are stable and exported in dashboards/index.yaml (used by incident-bot and the console deep links). - Alert rule names and labels match the monitor identity strings expected by the controller: monitor_kind in {latency_p95, error_rate}, plus route/model/region/customer_tier.

Testing: - jsonnet render + grafana dashboard validation (UID uniqueness, required templating variables present) - promtool rule check + unit tests for alert expressions (golden snapshots of rendered rules) - manual preview in staging Grafana: verified templating works for a known route+model and that missing-label panels light up for legacy metrics.

Rollout plan: This will ship behind the existing observability-pack release process. Once merged and deployed to staging, SRE will validate the panels during the game day (ENG-2323). After confirming monitor identity stability, the rollout-controller can start linking to these dashboards for auto-rollback events.

Notes: This PR intentionally does not change telemetry emission. Missing labels and cardinality issues are tracked separately (INT-3310 / ENG-2322).
commits: observability/rollouts: add SLO overview + drilldown dashboards
observability/rollouts: add monitor health dashboard (freshness, missing labels, query errors)
alerts/rollouts: add latency + error breach templates (warn/page)
alerts/rollouts: add monitor stale + label missing ticket alerts
docs: add rollout SLO dashboard/alert usage notes + links for console/oncall
ci_checks: Checks: jsonnet-lint (pass), dashboards-render (pass), grafana-validate (pass), promtool-check (pass), alert-rule-unit-tests (pass), repo-lint (pass). Reruns: grafana-validate initially failed due to duplicate UID (fixed by regenerating UID for drilldown dashboard); passed on rerun.
conversation:
Allison Grant (review): The label set in the queries needs to match ADR-0147 exactly. I still see a couple panels grouping by `tier` not `customer_tier`. Also: can we ensure we always include `deployment_mode` so Dedicated/Hosted don’t get mixed? Sergio Costa (author): Good catch. Updated templating vars to use `customer_tier` everywhere and added `deployment_mode` to the default selector. I also added a small panel note explaining when to filter by deployment_mode to reduce confusion for oncall.

Nadia Rahman (review): For the p95 latency panels, please avoid `histogram_quantile` directly on raw buckets without a recording rule; it’s too expensive at high cardinality. Do we have the `route_latency_ms_bucket:rate5m` recording rule available? Sergio Costa (author): Swapped to the existing `*_bucket:rate5m` recording rule where present, and added a fallback query (flagged as “expensive”) only on the drilldown dashboard. Alerts use the recording rules only.

Miles Thornton (review): Monitor stale alert should not page by default; we saw this during the Feb incident that a monitoring gap can cause cascading actions. Make sure this is ticket-only and surfaced clearly on the monitor health dashboard. Sergio Costa (author): Agreed. Set MonitorStale severity=ticket, added explicit dashboard panel “Controller-safe verdict: UNKNOWN when stale” and linked to the runbook section about fail-open vs fail-closed.

Benji Okafor (review): Can you confirm the alert labels line up with what rollout-controller will query? It expects a stable `monitor_kind` label + route/model/region/customer_tier. Sergio Costa (author): Yes—added `monitor_kind` to all templates and updated rule naming to be deterministic. Also added dashboards/index.yaml entries with stable UIDs for deep-linking.

Aisha Bello (review): Error-rate definition: are we counting 429s? For SLO rollback we generally exclude throttling from the service-level error budget. Sergio Costa (author): Updated error queries to include 5xx + gateway/internal errors and explicitly exclude 429 by default. Added a toggle variable on the drilldown dashboard to optionally include 429 for investigations.

Final approvals: Allison Grant (approved), Nadia Rahman (approved), Miles Thornton (approved).
release_notes: Adds Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert templates for rollout SLO monitoring (latency p95 and error-rate) aligned with ADR-0147 label contract; intended for auto-rollback deep links and oncall workflows.
